newsitem.title: JAPAN: KDD to offer cut-rate domestic phone service.
newsitem.headline: KDD to offer cut-rate domestic phone service.

text.p: Japan's international carrier Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co (KDD) will make a thrust into the huge domestic telecoms market later this month, offering long-distance service to corporate users at rates it says will undercut its rivals.
KDD said on Wednesday that it would launch its domestic phone service on July 26, initially offering its 2,700 leased-line users both domestic and international phone services at low rates.
"Because we will be the latest to make an entry into the domestic phone market, our tariffs should be the most competitive," KDD director Hideo Katsube told a news conference.

KDD dominates Japan's small international call market, but telecommunications deregulation, part of Japan's sweeping market reforms, has forced KDD to move into the huge but harshly competitive domestic call market.

Deregulation spurred telecom titan Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp and the world's big carriers to enter Japan's international call market, and their presence is expected to squeeze KDD's profitability later this year.

KDD's move into the domestic services, however, will expand its customer base, as the pool of phone users in the domestic call market numbers some 60 million compared with only six million in the international call market.
KDD's Katsube said fees for long-distance call service for its leased-line users would be 51 percent lower than those at NTT.
KDD will also start offering high-speed digital leased-line services in 14 areas of Japan at rates about 20 percent below those offered by NTT, Katsube said.

Users of KDD's 1,500 public phones will also be able to make international and domestic calls using an IC (integrated circuit) card beginning on July 26. KDD plans to increase the number of such public phones to 2,200 by March 1998, he said.
Households, meanwhile, will be able to make domestic phone calls through KDD beginning around April 1998.
KDD president Tadashi Nishimoto has said his company's domestic rates would be lower than any of its rivals, including NTT, DDI Corp and Japan Telecom.
Despite the bold price moves, however, some analysts question whether KDD will be able to turn a profit in domestic services.
"The charges announced today are very competitive," said Hironobu Sawake, an analyst at Nikko Research Centre. "But whether KDD's profitability will improve in the future is a different matter."

Amid intensified competition, KDD's market share was whittled down to 66 percent in the 1996/97 fiscal year from 67.9 percent the year before, the Nihon Keizai Shimbun business daily said in a survey.
But KDD's share price has been on the rise since June, as investors were cheered by the carrier's entry into domestic services. KDD's share price closed at 8,670 yen on Wednesday, up 320 yen.
